While most modules produced by First Solar in 2024 were Series 6, more than half the modules produced in the United States were Series 7. This ratio is expected to increase in 2025 as the Series 7 facility announcements documented in Figure 38 come online. First Solar indicates that Series 7 modules produced in the United States have 100% domestic sources for components listed in the U.S. Treasury domestic content guidance (First Solar 2024e).38 Thin-film PV technologies produced in the United States qualify for a 45X MPTC with a value of $170/kW for production and shipment of the wafer, cell, and module. Unlike c-Si PV dc technologies, these steps occur in a single facility for CdTe PV. Section 3.3.4 presents the impacts of these credits on manufacturing value. For the U.S. production of 6.3 GW CdTe PV dc in 2024, this would correspond to a total 45X MPTC value of approximately $1.1 billion. Based on press releases for the new U.S. facilities, we estimate the labor intensity for CdTe module production to be approximately 200 full-time jobs per annual GW of U.S. production dc (Kennedy 2023; First Solar 2022, 2021). This corresponds to approximately 1,300 total U.S. jobs for 2024 U.S. production levels. One domestic closure in 2024 was Toledo Solar (Norman 2024), which had purchased older CdTe PV production equipment with the intention of initially producing 100 MW /yr of dc smaller-format CdTe modules for residential and nonutility markets (Pickerel 2020). 3.3.3 Imports/Exports of CdTe Modules Figure 39 shows U.S. PV imports other than c-Si39 during 2022–2024 for any country supplying over 50 MW of imports in 2024. Most U.S. imports originated from India, Malaysia, and dc Vietnam, the three non-U.S. locations where CdTe modules are produced (Figure 38). While First Solar’s Vietnamese and Malaysian CdTe module manufacturing facilities remain active, U.S. non-c-Si module imports from those countries fell 15% from 2023 to 2024; over the same period, imports of non-c-Si modules from India grew from less than 11 MW to over 1 GW , dc dc which we attributable to the opening of First Solar’s 3 GW plant in India in early 2024. The dc data in Figure 38 and Figure 39 suggest most of global CdTe production is being imported into the United States. CdTe PV imports into the United States are not affected by the same tariffs and restrictions as c-Si PV. CdTe PV is specifically excluded from Section 201 tariffs and is not as directly affected by AD/CVD rates or UFLPA. There is high probability for demand in India for Indian-produced CdTe PV, because the country has a large utility-scale PV market supported by the government. CdTe PV is eligible for India’s Approved List of Models and Manufacturers for project development and Production-Linked Incentive for PV manufacturing. India also has tariffs on module and cell imports into India (40% and 25%, respectively) (Feldman, Zuboy, Dummit, Stright, et al. 2025).
